creation.initialPrompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Create a NEW ORIGINAL anatomy illustration, not a copied atlas plate, photograph, MRI, measurement plot or detached anatomical object.
Primary request: a simplified MEDIAN SAGITTAL SECTION OF AN ADULT HUMAN BRAIN, with the CORPUS CALLOSUM highlighted IN ITS ANATOMICAL LOCATION. Anterior LEFT, posterior RIGHT. Prioritize correct gross relationships and readable labels; omit uncertain fine anatomy.
Format: landscape 4:3, approximately 1536x1152. White background. Fill the image with a LARGE brain section and large labels, with modest margins and NO large empty lower half.
Style: clear restrained medical textbook illustration with light matte shading and thin quiet outlines. The cerebral hemisphere is pale neutral grey. Its broad normal medial outline is visible; avoid a tangled or decorative gyral pattern. Include only simple low-contrast gross silhouettes of brainstem inferiorly and cerebellum posterior to it at lower RIGHT. No cerebellar arbor vitae, internal brainstem nuclei, vessels, cranial nerves, pituitary, thalamic details, fornix, septum, or labelled ventricular system. The unspecified deep central tissue is a plain pale-grey schematic field, NOT a fabricated hollow cavity. Fine surrounding anatomy is deliberately omitted. NO invented detailed anatomy.
Highlight the corpus callosum as ONE CONTINUOUS golden-yellow C-shaped band embedded centrally within the medial hemisphere, below the medial cortical mantle. Its anterior-posterior length is approximately 45–50 percent of the cerebral hemisphere's length: it must NOT span most of the brain. Leave ample surrounding brain in front, above and behind it. The genu lies well behind the frontal pole and the splenium lies well before the occipital pole. The corpus callosum is separated from the cortex immediately above by a narrow, subtle callosal sulcus; do NOT highlight the cingulate gyrus instead. Do NOT draw a second duplicated C-shaped white band.
Callosal geometry: rounded thicker GENU at the LEFT anterior bend; very THIN short tapering ROSTRUM extends rightward/posteriorly from the lower inner side of the genu, below it, like a small flat beak (never a thick descending hook). Long gently arched superior TRUNCUS/BODY, thinner than genu and splenium; narrowed posterior ISTHMUS just before a rounded thicker SPLENIUM on the RIGHT. No sharp physical boundaries between segments; keep one continuous golden band. No invented longitudinal fiber striations or tubular cable surface.
Large dark navy sans serif callout labels, each exactly once. Use short German/Latin and English medical terms, no tiny paragraphs:
"1  Rostrum"
"2  Genu"
"3  Truncus / Body"
"4  Isthmus"
"5  Splenium"
These medical names are shared by German and English except Truncus/Body, which must appear together.
Five clean thin non-crossing leader lines with small dark terminal dots ON the correct highlighted tissue. Label 1 terminates on the thin posteriorly pointing beak beneath the genu, 2 on the rounded anterior bend, 3 on the central superior arch, 4 on the narrow posterior transition before the bulb, 5 on the rounded posterior bulb. Keep the leader endpoints unambiguous and DO NOT let labels or lines hide the tissue.
Top heading in large text: "Corpus callosum"
Small subtitle: "Mediansagittal · Midsagittal"
At bottom left "Anterior", bottom right "Posterior".
No other labels, numbers, measurement lines, logos, publication credits or watermarks. Do not add a separate enlarged callosal inset. This must clearly show WHERE the corpus callosum sits in a simplified sagittal brain, with only reliable gross contextual anatomy.
creation.correctionPrompt:
Edit this original illustration for ANATOMICAL SIMPLIFICATION AND CORRECTION.
Keep: the overall midsagittal brain silhouette, anterior LEFT/posterior RIGHT orientation, golden highlighted corpus callosum in its central location and at its current overall scale, the large readable navy labels 1–5, heading and orientation words. Keep the continuous superior callosal arch, the genu, posterior isthmus and rounded splenium.
Two REQUIRED corrections:
1. ROSTRUM: remove the current thick golden hook hanging downward from the inferior genu. Replace it with a MUCH THINNER, SHORT, FLAT, sharply tapering posteriorly directed beak immediately beneath/behind the lower genu. It should extend RIGHTWARD nearly horizontally and taper to a fine POINT, not curve down, not end with a rounded tip. It is about one-quarter the thickness of the central callosal body and much thinner than the genu. Update the endpoint of label "1 Rostrum" so it touches this thin beak, not the genu. Keep label 2 on the rounded anterior genu.
2. Simplify the surrounding brain radically: use a FLAT, UNIFORM PALE-GREY sagittal tissue field with only the broad outer hemisphere shape and minimal broad superficial contour hints. DELETE ALL the grey internal ovals, central nuclei, arches below the highlighted band, rounded central mass, small basal knobs, stalks, pituitary-like objects, fornix-like bands, ventricular-looking cavities, fine ridges and decorative 3D textures. This is a schematic section, so leave the deep grey tissue field UNPARTITIONED and UNSPECIFIED. The only clearly outlined INTERNAL anatomical structure must be the golden corpus callosum, with a narrow subtle sulcus just above it. Do not invent details to fill the field. Keep brainstem and cerebellum only as simple low-contrast outer silhouettes in their correct inferior/posterior positions; remove their internal texture and folia. No labelled neighboring structures.
Visual target: a clear simplified anatomical teaching illustration, closer to a restrained clean 2D medical drawing with light shading than a photorealistic 3D brain. Readability and correct callosal shape matter more than realistic texture. The central grey field must NOT look like a hollow empty hole or a fabricated giant ventricle.
Keep all text exactly spelled: "Corpus callosum", "Mediansagittal · Midsagittal", "1 Rostrum", "2 Genu", "3 Truncus / Body", "4 Isthmus", "5 Splenium", "Anterior", "Posterior". Leader lines remain non-crossing and land on the correct GOLDEN structure. No other labels or details.

scope: Original simplified midsagittal brain illustration with the corpus callosum highlighted in anatomical context.

initialDraftRejected: The rostrum was too thick and hooked downward.
The surrounding deep-brain details exceeded the intended simplified scope.
acceptedImageChecks: Anterior is left and posterior is right.
The highlighted callosal band is continuous and lies centrally within the hemisphere, below the medial cortical mantle.
The callosal band occupies roughly half the anteroposterior extent of the cerebral outline, with brain visible anterior, superior and posterior to it.
The rostrum is a thin posteriorly tapering beak beneath the genu; the genu is rounded; the body forms the superior arch; the posterior isthmus narrows before the splenium.
All five callout dots lie on their corresponding highlighted callosal portions, rather than on adjacent tissue.
Fine internal brain structures, vessels, fibre tracts and cerebellar internal details are omitted; the surrounding grey field is schematic.
The label Truncus / Body gives the German/Latin and English term; the other short medical segment names are shared by both languages. Full translated terminology remains in the HTML legend.
review.limits: A simplified gross-anatomy teaching illustration. Surrounding contours are schematic and are not intended as a map of individual gyri or deep structures. This visual cross-check is not an independent specialist certification.
